upstream.name: Matt Pocock's skills
upstream.attribution: Skills by Matt Pocock, MIT licence. Links go to the repository at a pinned revision.

skills.name: grill-me
skills.job: A front-door interview that classifies the work, plans rounds of questions and records each decision.
skills.status_note: My own skill, built from upstream's grilling. Not published; the upstream skill of the same name is a three-line stub, so it is not linked.

skills.name: grilling
skills.job: A relentless interview: walk the open decisions in rounds, each with a recommended answer.

skills.name: grill-with-docs
skills.job: The same interview, plus keeping the project's glossary and decision records current.

skills.name: domain-modeling
skills.job: Sharpen vague terms into a shared glossary and record the few decisions worth an ADR.

skills.name: to-spec
skills.job: Turn the conversation so far into a written specification. No new interview.

skills.name: to-tickets
skills.job: Break a specification into thin end-to-end slices, each stating what blocks it.

skills.name: wayfinder
skills.job: Plan work too big for one session as a map of decision tickets, resolved one at a time.
skills.difference: Same map model. My copy lets the model start it itself and predates several upstream additions, such as fresh-context research agents and the rule that map tickets carry only Wayfinder labels.

skills.name: implement-spec
skills.job: Build a whole specification and its tickets on one integration branch with parallel subagents.

skills.name: implement
skills.job: Build one ticket in one session, test-first, then review.

skills.name: tdd
skills.job: Red, green, refactor at agreed seams.
skills.difference: Same loop. I reuse test seams already agreed in the plan and ask again only when a new seam would change what the code promises.

skills.name: code-review
skills.job: Review a change on two separate axes: repository standards and fidelity to the spec.
skills.difference: Same two axes. Mine drops the tracker prerequisite, adds an optional browser-walkthrough evidence mode, and predates upstream's instruction to start each review sub-agent fresh.

skills.name: diagnosing-bugs
skills.job: Build a fast, repeatable failing signal first, then test ranked hypotheses.

skills.name: prototype
skills.job: Build a throwaway to answer one design question, then keep only the decision.

skills.name: research
skills.job: Parallel research: one subagent per question, then a separate synthesizer writes one report.
skills.status_note: Upstream has a skill called research that works differently (one background agent, one file); that is not this one.

skills.name: pm-cold-reader
skills.job: Have a reader with no context test a shareable document, in fresh contexts, until the findings stop changing.
skills.status_note: Described in my own words in the guides.

skills.name: shutdown
skills.job: Close out a session from a ledger of what happened: check repository sync, record decisions, add evidence to the tickets worked, and move one to review only when independent verification is pinned to the exact commit.
skills.status_note: It closes a session; it does not retrieve earlier decisions or reconcile changes.

skills.name: recall
skills.job: Answer 'why did we decide this' by searching several layers of notes and decision records, filtering out superseded ones and citing sources.
skills.status_note: Read-only: it offers to save a durable answer and never writes on its own.

skills.name: reconcile
skills.job: Detect what moved across the board, task lists, repository backlogs and meeting notes since the last baseline, say 'unknown' for anything it cannot read, and route each discrepancy to the skill that owns the fix.
skills.status_note: It detects and routes; it resolves nothing itself.

skills.name: handoff
skills.job: Turn the current conversation into a note a fresh agent can continue from, linking specs and commits instead of copying them and redacting secrets.
skills.status_note: Agent to agent; not the output of a close-out.

guides.task: I have an idea and I am not sure what to build
The project is too big and too foggy to plan in one sitting

Something is broken and I cannot reproduce it reliably
I want an agent to do real work without handing it the keys
guides.source_status: The shape, ready, admit, build, review and verify roles are private and unpublished. This guide is an original explanation; it links no instruction text.

guides.task: I need to understand a question before I decide anything
I wrote something for people who were not in the room
I am coming back to a project after time away

intro.examples: Every example below is synthetic. They follow one invented project, an in-house tool for comparing plate-reader assay runs, so you can see how the methods connect. No outcome, number, person or organisation in them is real.
intro.sources: Links go to the public upstream skills at one pinned revision. Where I run a different version, the entry says what I changed. My own versions are private: the guides describe what they do in my own words and publish none of their text.
